newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's wealthy said avoiding donation appeal.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's wealthy said avoiding donation appeal.

text.p: President Suharto has asked Indonesia's wealthy why they have ignored a government appeal to donate two percent of their profits to alleviate poverty, the official Antara news agency said on Sunday.

Speaking to more than 300 of Indonesia's wealthiest individuals on Saturday at the Bogor Palace, Suharto said only half of the country's 11,025 high-bracket taxpayers had contributed to a special poverty alleviation scheme.
"I want to know why only half of you have been able to contribute to the scheme. Do you have difficulties?" he asked.
"If so, I will help you. The director-general for taxes and customs will help businessmen having difficulty in the counting of their taxes," Suharto said.

The 1995 appeal for donations to the government's poverty alleviation programme was issued in the form of a presidential decree and addressed to private companies and individuals with an after-tax income of more than 100 million rupiah ($43,000) a year.
"Compliance with the decree is not compulsory. But as human beings, we have a moral responsiblity to help the poor and reduce the social disparities in the community," Suharto said.

The gap between rich and poor was seen by some analysts as one of the factors behind a number of recent disturbances in Indonesia including rioting in Jakarta on July 27. At least five people died in the riots, the worst in the capital in more than 20 years.

The disturbances began after police seized the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) but rioters later singled out government buildings, banks and luxury car showrooms, burning more than 100 vehicles.
